name: Seattle
tagline: Pacific Northwest Tech Hub with Coffee, Rain, and Mountain Views
description: Seattle offers FIRE retirees a unique blend of tech-driven culture, stunning natural beauty, and urban sophistication. With no state income tax, world-class healthcare from systems like UW Medicine and Swedish, and easy access to the Cascades and Puget Sound, it rewards those who embrace the drizzle. The cost of living is steep, but the quality of life — from Pike Place Market mornings to Olympic Mountain sunsets — is hard to match.

quickFacts.visa: No visa required for US citizens
quickFacts.internetSpeed: 200-1000 Mbps fiber widely available via CenturyLink and Xfinity
quickFacts.safetyRating: Moderately Safe — typical large US city with safe residential neighborhoods
quickFacts.nearestAirport: Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (SEA) — 25 min from downtown
quickFacts.climate: Oceanic with mild, wet winters (3-8°C) and dry, warm summers (18-27°C). Overcast 200+ days per year but less total rainfall than many East Coast cities.

1M.lifestyle: A careful but comfortable Pacific Northwest life. Housing is a modest studio in a residential neighborhood like Beacon Hill, Columbia City, or Northgate, priced around the citywide studio average and outside the pricey downtown core. Seattle's genuinely usable transit — an ORCA pass covering Link light rail and Metro buses — keeps a car off the budget entirely, the biggest lean-budget advantage the city offers. Cooking at home is the norm, with pho and teriyaki in the International District and indie-roaster coffee as affordable outings, while Discovery Park, Pike Place, and the waterfront supply free recreation. Washington's zero state income tax stretches every dollar; the persistent October-to-May drizzle is the main trade-off.

3M.lifestyle: A comfortably affluent city life in a modern one-bedroom in a walkable neighborhood like Capitol Hill, Ballard, Fremont, or Queen Anne. Dining out regularly across Seattle's strong seafood and coffee scene, a hybrid SUV for weekend access to Mount Rainier and the San Juans, and a ski pass at Crystal Mountain all fit easily, alongside a solid private health plan through UW Medicine or Swedish. With no state income tax, the combination of urban dining and culture with immediate mountains, water, and islands is the core appeal — and it comes without financial strain.

10M.lifestyle: The top of Seattle living, anchored by a luxury waterfront or downtown high-rise residence with Puget Sound or Cascade views. A private chef several nights a week, a luxury vehicle with car service, full household help, and elite concierge medicine are routine, alongside first-class travel and patron-level involvement in the Seattle Opera and the symphony. Weekend escapes to the San Juans or the Cascades need no planning, and Washington's zero income tax leaves the full budget intact. Established, nature-oriented wealth in one of the country's most scenic cities.
